sentence: She looked up the word in the dictionary
explanation: <Look up> significa buscar información. Es separable: 'looked the word up' también es correcto.

sentence: He came across an old photo in the drawer
explanation: <Come across> significa encontrar algo por casualidad.

sentence: They put off the meeting until next Monday
explanation: <Put off> significa posponer. Es separable: 'put the meeting off' también es correcto.

sentence: We need to figure out a solution to this problem
hint: Subject + need to + phrasal verb + object
explanation: <Figure out> significa encontrar la respuesta. Es separable: 'figure a solution out' también es correcto.

sentence: She turned down the invitation to the party
explanation: <Turn down> significa rechazar. Es separable: 'turned the invitation down' también es correcto.

sentence: He ran into his old teacher at the supermarket
explanation: <Run into> significa encontrarse con alguien de forma inesperada.

sentence: They called off the football match because of the rain
explanation: <Call off> significa cancelar. Es separable: 'called the football match off' también es correcto.

sentence: She takes after her mother in many ways
explanation: <Take after> significa parecerse a un familiar.

sentence: We should look into this matter more carefully
hint: Subject + modal + phrasal verb + object + adverb
explanation: <Look into> significa investigar o examinar.

sentence: He brought up an interesting point during the discussion
explanation: <Bring up> significa mencionar un tema. Es separable: 'brought an interesting point up' también es correcto.

sentence: She got over her cold after a few days of rest
explanation: <Get over> significa recuperarse de una enfermedad o dificultad.

sentence: They set up a new business in the city centre
explanation: <Set up> significa establecer algo nuevo. Es separable: 'set a new business up' también es correcto.

sentence: She hung up the phone before I could say goodbye
explanation: <Hang up> significa colgar el teléfono.

sentence: We checked in at the hotel late at night
explanation: <Check in> significa registrarse en un hotel.

sentence: Please check out before eleven in the morning
explanation: <Check out> significa dejar el hotel tras pagar la cuenta.

sentence: He never gives up when things get difficult
hint: Subject + adverb + phrasal verb + subordinate clause
explanation: <Give up> significa rendirse.

sentence: Students must hand in their homework on Friday
hint: Subject + modal + phrasal verb + object + time
explanation: <Hand in> significa entregar un trabajo.

sentence: Despite the noise, she carried on with her work
hint: Adverbial phrase + subject + phrasal verb (past) + object
explanation: <Carry on> significa continuar haciendo algo.

sentence: The guide pointed out several historical buildings
explanation: <Point out> significa señalar algo. Es separable.

sentence: Hold on a second, I need to find my keys
explanation: <Hold on> significa esperar un momento.
